papers.title: Recursive Recovery
papers.current_ceiling: A bounded methods/provenance claim about executable negative recovery is supported; general methodology effectiveness is not.
post_matrix_updates: Canonical PDF production has improved after #1731, but that is publication infrastructure rather than new science.
load_bearing_adverse: No existing gate licenses a broad effectiveness claim.
The proposed at-least-three-domain objective-verifier successor has never run.
Readiness and internal identifiers contain legacy ORION-02 aliasing that must be documented without rewriting frozen bytes.
papers.strongest_remaining_gap: The method has not been tested for correct recovery, false recovery and resource savings across independent objective-verifier domains.
papers.decisive_question: Does recursive negative recovery reduce verified recovery cost without increasing false recovery across theorem proving, software repair and the current native domain?
papers.maximum_claim_if_supported: Recursive recovery is a domain-general, verifier-safe strategy for recovering from failed research or computational actions under bounded evidence.
papers.hypothesis_or_theorem: Against resource-matched retry and domain-native recovery baselines, the frozen recursive policy should preserve verifier correctness and lower expected recovery cost in at least three qualitatively distinct domains.
papers.population_or_universe: Eligible failed episodes from E12 Lean/mathlib4, E3 Defects4J and one prospectively pinned native ORION recovery family, disjoint by theorem/project/task family.
papers.unit_of_analysis: One failed episode with its admissible recovery actions and objective verifier.
historical_only_inputs: All episodes used to design the existing bounded method
design: Extract failures and fixes without exposing held-out resolutions to the policy.
Map each domain to a common action/receipt schema while preserving native verifier semantics.
Compare exactly the same failure episodes and resource caps across policies.
Keep unrecoverable and misleading-success cases visible.
Bind every recovered state to the verifier output and causal action sequence.
baselines: Blind retry with the same action.
Oracle lower bound that knows the successful action only for analysis.
primary_endpoints: False recovery or verifier laundering, with zero as a noncompensatory gate.
negative_controls: Injected verifier false-positive signal that the policy must not trust.
Recovery action that improves a proxy while failing the native verifier.
Receipt with a missing causal step.
analysis_plan: Hierarchical paired analysis by episode and domain.
Competing-risk treatment of timeout versus incorrect recovery.
Predeclare cost weights or report the full resource vector without scalarization.
A cross-domain claim requires the same policy and terminal semantics in every domain.
papers.power_or_exhaustion_rule: Use all eligible frozen episodes up to a prospectively fixed resource budget; establish the minimum domain-level episode count by simulation on design-only episodes.
papers.success_gate: Zero false recoveries, noninferior verified success and lower recovery resources than every feasible donor baseline in all three domains or under a preregistered hierarchical criterion.
papers.refutation_gate: Any false recovery defeats the safety headline; domain-specific parity limits the claim to the bounded provenance object.
papers.cannot_check_gate: CANNOT_CHECK if fixes leak into inputs, native verifier results cannot be reproduced or domain mappings change after outcomes.
papers.authority_required: Native objective verifiers plus an independently implemented replay/checker; domain experts audit the mapping, not the outcomes.

active_lane.collision_rule: No active external successor was identified; keep the bounded readiness package immutable.

immediate_safe_actions: Regenerate the receipt index against the final bounded claim set.
Define the common recovery schema and native-verifier adapters.
Resolve the legacy ORION-02 alias through an additive mapping note.
forbidden_actions: Do not claim broad recovery effectiveness from provenance correctness.
Do not substitute proxy success for native verifier success.
Do not rewrite frozen legacy identifiers in place.
papers.journal_bar: A top-tier systems/methods paper needs objective correctness, domain diversity, strong native baselines, full resource accounting and a noncompensatory false-recovery gate.
papers.sibling_boundary: Owns recovery after failure; epistemic state reconstruction belongs to ORION-11.
